name: The Roloson household at 2109 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_roloson_robert_w

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 2109 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 2109 Robert W. Roloson.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 2109, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The three live-in staff and one child it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 are on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. The 1910 census was not read. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: Robert W. Roloson
persons.note: The 1900 census lists Robert Roloson here as head, born April 1840, widowed, board of Trade (ED 40, sheet 14B, line 58, leaf n821).

persons.name: Robert Roloson

born.note: The census gives October 1879, age 20 on 1 June 1900.

occupation.note: Written as "At school" in the occupation column on 1 June 1900.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the house, as a son of the head (at school); born October 1879 (the figures are hard to read), in Illinois, single. The 1904 Blue Book names no children, so a child at home in 1900 is placed here in 1904 by inference.

persons.name: Mary Burns

born.note: The census gives August 1875, age 24 on 1 June 1900.

occupation.note: Written as "Parlor maid" in the occupation column on 1 June 1900.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the house, as a servant (parlor maid); born August 1875 (the figures are hard to read), in Ireland, came to the United States in 1891, single. Servants changed places often, so this records who worked here in 1900; no source read says whether this person was still here on 1 July 1904. Part of the name is hard to read on the sheet; this is the best reading.
